hints.content:
The basic function $\cos(x)$ has a maximum point at $(0,1)$ and intersects its midline at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right)$.

$\qquad$![](${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/045d194412b500fdd873c28902f2f903.png)

Let's transform $\pink{\cos(x)}$ to $\blue{5\cos(2x-3\pi)+2}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

The transformation from $\pink{\cos(x)}$ to $\green{\cos(2x)}$ is a horizontal shrink by a factor of $2$, so the intersection point's horizontal distance from the origin is shrunk from $0.5\pi$ to $0.25\pi$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

The transformation from $\green{\cos(2x)}$ to $\red{5\cos(2x)}$ is a vertical stretch by a factor of $5$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is stretched from $1$ to $5$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, one) and a point on the midline next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, zero). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, one) and a point at the midline next to the mentioned point around (pi over four, zero).

A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, one) and a point at the midline next to the mentioned point around (pi over four, zero). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, five) and a point at the midline next to the mentioned point around (pi over four, zero).

hints.content: The transformation from $\red{5\cos(2x)}$ to $\blue{5\cos(2x-3\pi)+2}$, which is equivalent to $5\cos{\large(}2(x-1.5\pi){\large)}+2$, is a translation to the right by $1.5\pi$ units and a translation upwards by $2$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the maximum point is now at $\left(1.5\pi,7\right)$ and the intersection with the midline is at $(1.75\pi,2)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. There is a point on the graph at a maximum at (three pi over two, seven) and a point on the midline next to the mentioned point at (one and seventy five hundredths pi, two).

question.content:
**Graph $f(x)=5\cos(2x-3\pi)+2$ in the interactive widget.**  
*Note that one moveable point always defines an extremum point in the graph and the other point always defines a neighbouring intersection with the midline.*
